updates.content:
Title: Some users in the United States may be unable to access Microsoft 365 services

User impact: Users in the United States may be unable to access Microsoft 365 services.

Current status: We're reviewing service monitoring telemetry and associated reports to isolate the root cause, in order to develop a remediation plan.

Scope of impact: Impact is specific to users in the United States attempting to access Microsoft 365 services. This information may be updated as our investigation continues.

Next update by: Wednesday, September 16, 2026, at 3:30 PM UTC

We're reviewing service telemetry and investigating user reports of 502 and 503 errors when attempting to access Microsoft 365 services to further isolate the source of impact and determine our next remediation steps.
 
This quick update is designed to give the latest information on this issue.
 
Next update by: Wednesday, September 16, 2026, at 3:30 PM UTC

Title: Some users in the United States and United Kingdom may be unable to access Microsoft 365 services

User impact: Users in the United States and United Kingdom may be unable to access Microsoft 365 services.

Current status: We're reviewing service telemetry while investigating reports of users encountering 502 and 503 errors when accessing Microsoft 365 services. Recent user reports indicate the impact may be decreasing and we're continuing to analyze service health data to determine whether service conditions are improving and to isolate the source of impact.
 
Scope of impact: Impact is specific to users attempting to access Microsoft 365 services and users whose service requests are routed through the United States and United Kingdom regions. This information may be updated as our investigation continues.
 
Next update by: Wednesday, September 16, 2026, at 3:30 PM UTC

Title: Some users in the United States and United Kingdom may be unable to access Microsoft 365 services

User impact: Users in the United States and United Kingdom may be unable to access Microsoft 365 services.

More info: Impacted users may encounter 502 or 503 errors when attempting to access Microsoft 365 services.

Current status: Our investigation remains focused on the cause of the Single Sign-On (SSO) failures and associated 5xx errors. In parallel, we're reviewing upstream dependencies to determine whether they are contributing to the impact. While some affected customers have reported improvement in service availability, our investigation continues as we work towards a full resolution.

Start time: Wednesday, September 16, 2026, at 1:22 PM UTC

Next update by: Wednesday, September 16, 2026, at 4:30 PM UTC

The majority of impact reports have subsided, however, we continue to investigate. Specifically, we're reviewing multiple sections of the request flows, including IP filtering, upstream dependencies and service access paths associated with the reported Single Sign-On (SSO) failures.
 
This quick update is designed to give the latest information on this issue.

Current status: Impact reports continue to decrease. Our investigation has not identified any issues with core Microsoft 365 components. As part of our ongoing root cause analysis, we're focusing on the request paths and dependency conditions associated with the reported Single Sign-On (SSO) failures and 5xx errors, while continuing to monitor and confirm sustained recovery.

Title: Some users in the United States and United Kingdom may be unable to access Microsoft 365 services

User impact: Users in the United States and United Kingdom may have been unable to access Microsoft 365 services.

More info: Impacted users may have encountered 502 or 503 errors when attempting to access Microsoft 365 services.

Final status: We’ve thoroughly reviewed our telemetry and can confirm there were no issues within the Microsoft-managed environment, which remained healthy throughout this event. Scope of impact: Users in the United States and United Kingdom attempting to use Microsoft 365 services may have been impacted.
